name: Kellanova
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Makes snacks and cereals including Pringles, Cheez-It, Pop-Tarts and Kellogg's international cereal brands, sold in 180+ countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Mars, Incorporated (acquisition completed Dec 2025; delisted from NYSE)
capacity_detail: Acquired by Mars, deal completed 11 Dec 2025 at about USD 36bn (Bloomberg figure cited on Wikipedia); revenue USD 12.7bn in 2024
markets: Products manufactured and marketed in over 180 countries; large operations in the US and UK (Trafford Park).
rationale: Pringles is a global snack brand aimed at young audiences; F1's international fan base and trackside visibility suit impulse snack marketing.

name: WK Kellogg Co
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Makes Kellogg's breakfast cereals for North America, including Frosted Flakes, Froot Loops and Special K.
ownership: subsidiary of Ferrero (acquired Sep 2025; delisted from NYSE)
capacity_detail: Bought by Ferrero for USD 3.1bn, completed 26 Sep 2025; revenue USD 2.71bn in 2024
markets: North American cereal market: United States, Canada and the Caribbean.
rationale: Cereal brands need mass US family reach; F1's fast-growing US audience and Grand Prix races in Miami, Austin and Las Vegas offer that.

name: BSH Hausgeräte
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Europe's largest home appliance maker, selling Bosch, Siemens, Gaggenau, Neff and Thermador appliances in 50 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH (100% since Jan 2015)
markets: Present in 50 countries with 37 factories; markets include Europe, the US and Canada, India and Poland.
rationale: Premium appliance brands like Gaggenau and Thermador target affluent households; F1 hospitality and premium positioning fit high-end kitchen marketing.

name: Penguin Random House
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: The world's largest trade book publisher, issuing about 14,500 new titles a year across many countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Bertelsmann (100% since April 2020)
markets: US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, Germany, Spain, Hispanic America, Brazil, Asia and South Africa.
rationale: Publishes F1 driver memoirs and sports books through DK and Penguin; a content partnership could tie publishing to F1's storytelling boom.

name: bonprix
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Online and catalogue fashion retailer selling its own clothing and home textiles in more than 25 markets.
ownership: subsidiary of Otto Group (Michael Otto Foundation)
markets: More than 25 markets, mostly in Europe.
rationale: Value fashion brand with pan-European reach could use F1's growing female audience for brand awareness campaigns.

name: Geodis
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Global logistics group offering freight forwarding, contract logistics, distribution and road transport in 166 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of SNCF (100%; French state-owned)
markets: Present in 166 countries with about 53,000 employees; strong US presence (Nashville).
rationale: Rival logistics firms DHL and CEVA use F1 to show global capability; Geodis could match them with B2B hospitality and visibility.

name: Keolis
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Operates public transport networks including buses, trams, metros and trains for cities in many countries.
ownership: subsidiary of SNCF (70%), with La Caisse (CDPQ) 30%
markets: France, UK, US, Canada, Australia, India, China, Qatar, Dubai, the Nordics, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands and Ireland.
rationale: Bids for city transport contracts worldwide; F1 Grand Prix host cities are its clients, so hospitality could support government relationships.

name: Geopost
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: International parcel delivery group running DPD, Chronopost, Seur, BRT and Speedy across Europe and beyond.
ownership: subsidiary of La Poste (French state-owned postal group)
markets: Direct presence in 24 countries, mainly Europe; services in Asia, South Africa, India and Brazil via partners.
rationale: DPD competes with DHL, an F1 logistics partner; F1 visibility could lift DPD's consumer brand across European delivery markets.

name: Digitec Galaxus
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Switzerland's largest online retailer, selling electronics and general goods and expanding across Western Europe.
ownership: subsidiary of Migros (70%)
markets: Switzerland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands.
rationale: Galaxus is building awareness in new European markets against Amazon; F1's European fan base offers fast brand recognition.

name: PreZero
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Waste management and recycling company of the Schwarz Group, operating in Germany and several other European countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Schwarz Group
sponsorships: Naming rights to PreZero Arena, Sinsheim (TSG Hoffenheim, Bundesliga), since 2019; partnerships with Allianz Arena, Red Bull Arena Leipzig and the German Handball Bundesliga
markets: Germany, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden.
rationale: Already uses stadium sponsorships for brand-building; F1's sustainability programme and event waste needs fit a recycling partner.

name: Kaufland
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Hypermarket chain of the Schwarz Group with about 1,650 stores in Germany and Central and Eastern Europe.
ownership: subsidiary of Schwarz Group
markets: Germany, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Moldova, Poland, Romania and Slovakia.
rationale: Mass retailer in markets with strong F1 followings like Germany and Poland; F1 promotions could drive store traffic.

name: Tata AIG General Insurance
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Indian general insurer offering motor, health, travel, home and commercial insurance, a joint venture of Tata and AIG.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Sons (about 74%), with AIG about 26%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 11,408 crore in 2024 (article body; infobox gives INR 15,424 crore)
markets: Insurance customers across India.
rationale: Motor insurance is its core line; F1's fast-growing Indian audience and car-loving fans match its target customers.

name: Tata AIA Life Insurance
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Indian life insurer selling protection, savings and investment-linked policies, a joint venture of Tata Sons and AIA.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Sons (51%), with AIA Group 49%
markets: Life insurance customers across India.
rationale: Competes for affluent Indian savers; F1's premium image and growing Indian viewership could support brand trust and hospitality.

name: Tata Play
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: India's largest direct-to-home satellite TV provider, also offering bundled streaming and broadband services.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Group (70%), with Disney India 30%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 5,741 crore (about USD 610m) in fiscal 2026
markets: Pay-TV households across India; 21.3 million subscribers in March 2023.
rationale: A pay-TV platform needs premium sports content and audiences; F1 association could support subscriptions among India's growing motorsport fans.

name: Tata Advanced Systems
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Makes aerostructures, military vehicles, radars, drones and satellites, including parts for Lockheed Martin, Boeing and Airbus.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Sons (100%)
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 5,176 crore (about USD 550m) in FY24
markets: Indian defence customers plus global aerospace partners such as Lockheed Martin, Airbus and Boeing.
rationale: Precision aerospace engineering parallels F1 technology; an engineering partnership could aid recruitment and showcase capability, though defence limits fit.

name: General Logistics Systems (GLS)
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Parcel delivery network serving business and consumer shippers across Europe and North America, partnering in 50+ countries.
ownership: subsidiary of International Distribution Services, controlled by EP Group (Daniel Kretinsky) since 2025
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6bn for 2025-26 (IDS annual report, cited on Wikipedia)
markets: Parcel delivery across Europe and North America; more than 50 countries with partners.
rationale: Competes with DHL, an F1 logistics partner; F1 visibility could build GLS's brand in European and North American parcel markets.

name: BBC Studios
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Commercial arm of the BBC that produces, distributes and sells TV programmes and runs international channels.
ownership: subsidiary of the BBC (UK public corporation)
markets: Worldwide content sales and channels, with operations in Australia, Canada, India, Japan, Mexico, South Africa and Asia.
rationale: Runs Top Gear and global factual channels; F1 content partnerships could feed its motoring and documentary output worldwide.

name: Waitrose & Partners
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Premium British supermarket chain with about 330 shops, exporting own-label products to 52 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of John Lewis Partnership (employee-owned)
sponsorships: Past: Reading FC (2008-2015), England cricket team (2013-2016)
markets: Great Britain and the Channel Islands; exports to 52 countries; Middle East via Spinneys licence.
rationale: Affluent British shoppers overlap with F1's UK audience; British Grand Prix hospitality and premium food could fit the brand.

name: Moeve
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Spanish energy company, formerly Cepsa, refining and selling fuels, chemicals and green hydrogen, renamed Moeve in 2024.
ownership: subsidiary of Mubadala Investment Company (61.36% via Cepsa Holding), with The Carlyle Group 38.41%
sponsorships: Title sponsor of Liga F (Liga F Moeve); Spain national football team since 2007; past Toro Rosso F1 sponsor c.2011-2015
markets: Spain and Portugal, with operations in Algeria, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Peru, the UK and the Netherlands.
rationale: New Moeve brand needs awareness; it sponsored Toro Rosso before, and Spanish F1 enthusiasm (Madrid GP from 2026) makes a strong fit.

name: Nutreco
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Animal nutrition and fish feed company running Trouw Nutrition and Skretting, producing in 40 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of SHV Holdings (since 2015; delisted from Euronext)
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 7.5bn (key figures, SHV Annual Report 2025)
markets: Present in 40 countries with sales in over 90 countries.
rationale: B2B feed brand with global farm customers; limited consumer pull, but F1 hospitality could support distributor relationships.

name: Kiwa
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Testing, inspection and certification company with offices in 39 countries across Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Americas.
ownership: subsidiary of SHV Holdings (since 2021)
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 1.7bn (key figures, SHV Annual Report 2025)
markets: 39 countries across Europe, Asia-Pacific, North America and Latin America.
rationale: Growing by acquisition in certification markets; F1 hospitality could help win industrial and automotive clients, though brand pull is modest.

name: SHV Energy
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Distributes liquefied petroleum gas and other off-grid energy to homes and businesses in over 21 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of SHV Holdings
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 7.4bn (key figures, SHV Annual Report 2025)
markets: Over 21 countries across four continents.
rationale: LPG brands sell to rural homes and businesses; F1's sustainable-fuel story could suit its low-carbon fuels push, but fit is modest.

name: Stena Line
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: One of Europe's largest ferry operators, running passenger and freight routes across the North Sea, Baltic and Irish Sea.
ownership: subsidiary of Stena AB (Olsson family)
markets: Sweden, Denmark, Norway routes plus UK, Ireland, Germany, Netherlands, Poland, Latvia, Finland and France.
rationale: Carries fans to the British and Dutch Grands Prix; F1 travel packages and visibility could promote its car-ferry routes.

name: Puma Energy
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Midstream and downstream fuel company running storage terminals and service stations in about 34 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Trafigura (over 90%)
sponsorships: Local partner of CONMEBOL Libertadores and Sudamericana (2025); past Zambia International Rally
markets: About 34 countries on five continents, notably Africa, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Fuel retail brand in emerging markets with rally sponsorship history; F1 could lift its station brand in Latin America and Africa.

name: Symetra
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: US insurer selling life insurance, annuities, retirement plans and employee benefits through brokers and employers.
ownership: subsidiary of Sumitomo Life (acquired 2016 for USD 3.8bn)
capacity_detail: Founding partner and sponsor of the Seattle Kraken (NHL) since 2021; revenue USD 4.6bn in 2021
sponsorships: Seattle Kraken (NHL) founding partner since 2021; Seattle Storm (WNBA) jersey sponsor from 2019; Symetra Tour (LPGA development, 2012-2021)
markets: Life, annuity and benefits customers across the United States.
rationale: Already buys major-league sports deals to build national awareness; F1's growing US audience could extend that reach.

name: DERTOUR Group
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Tour operator and travel group of REWE, running package holiday brands and hotels, and expanded through buying Hotelplan.
ownership: subsidiary of REWE Group (co-operative)
markets: European source markets including Germany, Switzerland (Hotelplan), Austria and Central Europe, selling holidays worldwide.
rationale: F1 travel packages are a growth niche; a tour operator could sell Grand Prix trips and gain brand visibility across Europe.

name: PENNY
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: REWE Group's discount supermarket chain operating in Germany, Italy, Austria, Romania, the Czech Republic and Hungary.
ownership: subsidiary of REWE Group (co-operative)
capacity_detail: PENNY Germany revenue EUR 9.9bn and PENNY International EUR 8.6bn in 2025
markets: Germany, Italy, Austria, Romania, the Czech Republic and Hungary.
rationale: Discounter competing with Lidl and Aldi; F1 promotions in Germany, Italy and Hungary, all Grand Prix markets, could build traffic.

name: Henkell Freixenet
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Sparkling wine, wine and spirits producer behind Henkell, Freixenet and Mionetto, distributing Korbel globally since 2025.
ownership: subsidiary of Oetker-Gruppe (sparkling wine, wine and spirits division)
markets: Western Europe 32%, DACH 27%, Americas 21%, Eastern Europe 18% of sales; new units in Argentina, Croatia and Ireland in 2025.
rationale: Podium celebrations are sparkling-wine moments; rivals Moët, Mumm and Taittinger have used F1, so Freixenet or Mionetto could follow.

name: Radeberger Gruppe
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Germany's largest brewing group, owner of Radeberger, Jever and other beer and soft-drink brands.
ownership: subsidiary of Oetker-Gruppe
markets: Mainly Germany, with beer and alcohol-free drinks such as Jever Fun and Radeberger Alkoholfrei.
rationale: Its alcohol-free beers are growing; F1 allows 0.0 beer promotion, as Heineken does, giving a route to German fans.

name: Arvato Group
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Bertelsmann's services group providing supply chain, e-commerce logistics, IT and customer services in more than 30 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Bertelsmann (division of Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA)
markets: More than 30 countries; France and the United States are the most important markets outside Germany.
rationale: Runs e-commerce fulfilment for global brands; F1 B2B hospitality and visibility could support wins against DHL and CEVA, both F1 partners.

name: Denner
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Switzerland's largest discount supermarket chain, a subsidiary of the Migros co-operative group.
ownership: subsidiary of Migros (co-operative)
markets: Discount grocery stores across Switzerland.
rationale: Domestic discounter with limited international pull; F1 promotions could support Swiss customer campaigns, but fit is modest.

name: Medbase
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Swiss healthcare group of the Migros co-operative running medical centres, physiotherapy, dental practices and pharmacies.
ownership: subsidiary of Migros (co-operative)
markets: Healthcare services across Switzerland.
rationale: Sports medicine and physiotherapy offer a link to athlete performance, but its domestic Swiss footprint makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Croma (Infiniti Retail)
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Tata's consumer electronics retail chain with over 550 stores in more than 200 Indian cities and online sales.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Digital, wholly owned by Tata Sons
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 19,064 crore (about USD 2.0bn) in fiscal 2025 (year to March 2025)
markets: Over 550 stores in more than 200 Indian cities plus online.
rationale: Sells gadgets to young urban Indians, a core F1 growth audience; F1 tie-ins could support premium electronics launches.

name: Vibracoustic
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Supplies vehicle noise and vibration control parts such as mounts, bushings and air springs to carmakers worldwide.
ownership: subsidiary of Freudenberg Group (business group of Freudenberg & Co. KG, family-owned)
markets: About 40 locations in 17 countries supplying global vehicle makers.
rationale: Automotive supplier selling to carmakers; F1 engineering association and hospitality with OEM buyers mirror rivals like Tenneco and Brembo.

name: Freudenberg Home and Cleaning Solutions (Vileda)
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Makes household cleaning products under brands including Vileda, O-Cedar, Wettex, Marigold and Gimi.
ownership: subsidiary of Freudenberg Group (business group of Freudenberg & Co. KG, family-owned)
markets: Household cleaning brands Vileda, O-Cedar, Wettex, Marigold and Gimi sold in international markets.
rationale: Mass household brands need broad awareness; F1 is a weak but possible fit via family-audience campaigns in Europe.

name: OBI
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: German DIY and home improvement store chain with about 650 stores in ten European countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Tengelmann Group (about 74%), with Lueg Group holding the rest
markets: Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Italy, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
rationale: DIY retail draws male car enthusiasts; F1 visibility in Germany, Austria, Italy and Hungary could strengthen OBI against rival chains.

name: Bosch Rexroth
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: Makes hydraulics, electric drives, controls and linear motion technology for factory automation and mobile machinery.
ownership: subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH (wholly owned)
markets: Germany, Sweden, United States, Israel, Poland, Singapore, China and the wider Asia-Pacific region.
rationale: Precision motion and hydraulics engineering mirrors F1 technology; B2B hospitality with machine builders resembles rivals' use of F1, such as SKF and DMG MORI.

name: PrizePicks
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: US daily fantasy sports and prediction app where players pick athlete stat outcomes across major leagues.
ownership: subsidiary of Allwyn (62.3%, completed early 2026); Allwyn is about 78% held by KKCG and listed in Athens since March 2026
capacity_detail: Allwyn bought a 62.3% stake for about USD 1.5bn, deal announced Jan 2026 and completed
sponsorships: Official daily fantasy sports partner of the Atlanta Braves (MLB) since April 2024; State Farm Arena marketing partner (June 2024)
markets: Daily fantasy sports players across US states.
rationale: Sister company of F1 partner Allwyn; F1 driver-stat contests could extend its US sports audience to motorsport.

name: Oldenburgische Landesbank (OLB)
group: Subsidiaries of unlisted groups, family conglomerates and state groups
desc: North German bank serving private, business and corporate clients, bought by Crédit Mutuel's Targo Deutschland in January 2026.
ownership: subsidiary of Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale via TARGO Deutschland GmbH (100%, completed 2 Jan 2026)
markets: Retail and corporate banking in Germany, mainly Lower Saxony and northern Germany.
rationale: Regional bank with little international pull; F1 hospitality might help win corporate clients, but fit is weak.
